title: Deion Sanders Remains Uncommited with 2025 Colorado Starting QB - NewsBreak
text: One thing that is new for the Colorado Buffaloes with Deion Sanders coaching is figuring out who will be under center. During his first two years, he had his son, Shedeur Sanders, as the team’s starting quarterback and now has to find a new quarterback to lead the program. There are a couple of options that Sanders can choose from, as five-star true freshman Julian “JuJu” Lewis is joining the program as well as Liberty Flames transfer Kaidon Salter heading to Boulder this season. We got a bit of a revelation of what the Buffs could be doing with the quarterback position on Wednesday so let’s take a look at what Deion Sanders said. While speaking at the 2025 Big 12 Media Day, coach Deion Sanders would not commit to which one of the two quarterbacks, true freshman JuJu Watkins or transfer Kaidon Salter, will be the starting quarterback for the upcoming season. While not committing to either quarterback heading into the Big 12 Media Day and both Salter and Lewis being players at the event representing the program, Prime Time discussed how there’s even the possibility of seeing both in a game. “Yeah. Long as they’re doing their jobs and we’re winning. We definitely want to continue to develop JuJu, but Kaidon is unbelievable. Kaidon is off the chain. He’s been there, done that, he can get the job done. I wouldn’t have brought him here if I didn’t trust him. “But JuJu is coming around the mountain when he comes. And I love him, I love what he brings to the table. I don’t know how it’s going to play out, as long as it plays out. We can’t lose either way, with either of these two.” Salter took a step back in 2024 as he completed 147 of 261 (56.3%) of his passes for 1,886 yards with 15 passing touchdowns to six interceptions as well as 114 rushing attempts for 587 yards (5.1 yards per carry) wiht seven rushing touchdowns. It will be interesting to see who is under center for coach Deion Sanders when the team hosts the Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets on Aug. 29.
